findings.claim: `_attach_runs_minted_since` sweeps in any row from `runs` with `run_id > high_water AND batch_id IS NULL`, with no filter on repo and no lock — its own comment justifies this by claiming 'under K=1 nothing else can mint a run while one candidate's call is in flight' (lines 66-69), but K=1 is a property of this loop's own scheduling, not an exclusive lock on the shared ledger. The documented, supported `saffron cell` command (CLAUDE.md) also calls `create_run` with `batch_id=None` and can be run by the operator at any time, including while a batch is executing; if it (or a second batch, or a run against a different repo) mints a run inside the narrow window between the `high_water` read and a crashing runner's raise, that unrelated run's cost gets silently folded into this batch's `batch_spend`, corrupting the budget gate and the batch's recorded spend without any gate or test (all of which run single-process and synchronous) ever observing it.

`_attach_runs_minted_since` is scoped by `run_id > high_water AND batch_id IS NULL`, and the docstring justifies this scope by asserting 'Under K=1 nothing else can mint a run while one candidate's call is in flight' (lines 66-69). That is only true of this in-process loop; `runs.batch_id IS NULL` is also the steady-state left by `saffron cell` and `replay.py` (both documented in CLAUDE.md as ordinary, concurrently-usable commands) writing to the same shared `~/.saffron/ledger.db`. `high_water` is read via `_max_run_id`, which takes the MAX over the whole `runs` table with no repo scoping (line 46), and the window between that read and the runner's eventual exception spans the full duration of one cell's execution — long enough for an operator's manual `saffron cell` invocation against the same ledger file to mint an unrelated NULL-`batch_id` run with `run_id > high_water` in that window. On the next exception, that unrelated run gets swept into this batch's spend, silently corrupting `batch_spend` and the budget gate for a night the tests (all single-process, single ledger connection, no concurrent writer) cannot exercise.

Both clock-related tests (`test_the_until_deadline_is_read_from_an_injected_clock` and `test_the_clock_is_checked_before_a_task_still_inside_the_window`) drive exactly one candidate through `run_batch`, so neither can tell 'the deadline is checked once, before the loop starts' apart from 'the deadline is checked before every task.' Moving the `if until is not None and clock() >= until:` block from inside the `for` loop to just before it (still returning UNTIL/closing the batch the same way) keeps every existing test green — each supplies only a single candidate — while breaking the acceptance criterion that the deadline is 'compared before starting a task rather than during one' for every task: a batch that crosses `--until` only after its first candidate starts would then run every remaining candidate unbounded, since inside the loop only the budget and breaker would still be checked.
